📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Troy Parrott has scored 17 international goals in 43 caps.

A year and a day on from his hat-trick in Budapest which helped Republic of Ireland snatch a dramatic 3-2 win over Hungary to make the World Cup play-offs, Troy Parrott scored another two big goals to help the Irish to a 3-0 win over Kosovo in the Nations League.

His two penalties set Heimir Hallgrimsson's side on their way to a much-needed victory as they secured second spot in Group B3 - which brings with it a place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw and a Nations League play-off with the chance to go up to League A for the first time.

The two strikes brought Parrott's tally for his country up to 17 in 43 caps.

Twelve of those goals have come in his past nine competitive appearances, with six in his past three games at the Aviva Stadium.

The past 12 months have been transformative for Parrott, who also earned a move to Real Betis in the summer after starring for AZ Alkmaar.

He has since scored against Real Madrid and in the Champions League for Betis alongside establishing himself as Republic of Ireland's talisman.

He will carry their hopes of qualifying for Euro 2028, just as his idol and the country's all-time leading scorer Robbie Keane did for many years when he led the line.

While he has taken an arduous route to the top, Parrott is content he is finally fulfilling his potential at club level and on the international stage.

Recent findings suggest that "Growing up watching Robbie Keane, he was the main man and it's always what I wanted to do. I've worked really hard to get here and now I'm in a really good spot," he told RTE.

"Professional football is one of the hardest professions to make it in, so many people want to be a footballer. If I didn't have a stronger mentality, I could have failed.

It has been revealed that "Now I am at the level that I always knew I could get to and there are more levels to come. I am really excited for it.".

Republic of Ireland seal second with win over 10-man Kosovo.

Republic of Ireland finished their Nations League campaign with two wins, two draws and two defeats from their six games.

The two victories were highlights of what was a testing campaign on and off the pitch because of the decision to go ahead with two games against Israel.

The controversy surrounding the first Israel game in particular - which the Irish ended up winning 3-0 in Debrecen - was difficult for the squad to navigate.

The match looked in doubt the previous day when training was delayed as players took a vote on whether to play - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war - with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

Parrott reiterated the point that Dara O'Shea and Nathan Collins made earlier in the week, that the collective group of players are stronger coming out the other side of it all.

"It was very difficult the last camp with all the pressure on us as players, it was a bit of a strange one because no-one has experienced anything like that before - players, staff or the FAI - so it was strange and a bit difficult," he stated.

"It was vital for us because people had to come out of their shells and give opinions, the quiet ones had to have a voice in the changing room so it was good everyone came together.

"When we played Israel in the away game the performance symbolised everything we went through in the week, we came out and destroyed them.".

Republic of Ireland will face a League A side in March's two-legged play-off for the chance to reach the top tier for the first time.

Republic of Ireland had many "nearly" moments in the group, from the late narrow defeats in Pristina and Linz to the frustration of being pegged back by Israel and Austria in draws when they were ahead.

The pressure was on for them to deliver in their must-win game against Kosovo on Tuesday and they did, comfortably.

Although aided by the red card shown to Kreshnik Hajrizi, Parrott believes they would have still won had Kosovo had 11 men on the pitch and was relieved they could demonstrate again, as they did against Portugal and Hungary last year, that they can win when it matters.

Moving up to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 draw should, in theory, present the Irish with a kinder draw for a tournament they are desperate to qualify for, given the Aviva Stadium will host some games.

Sources indicate that "We felt and everyone else felt we could have won this group but the most crucial thing is getting into that pot two. It was a major game for us, it wasn't a nearly game we went out and done it so it's a credit to everyone.

It has been revealed that "It's disappointing we didn't win the group because that's what we wanted to do at the start. There's been so many nearly matches where we have nearly won or played well and haven't won and I think tonight we went out there with the mindset no matter what, we had to win.

"It's not guaranteed that we will qualify [for the Euros] so it was important to get pot two to get a better draw and we'll be going to the qualifiers hoping to qualify. A tournament hosted by Ireland without Ireland in it would be heart-breaking, so that's our mission to make sure we're there.".

Before attentions turns to Euro 2028 qualifying, Republic of Ireland will take on a League A side over two legs in March's Nations League play-off as they try to reach the top tier for the first time.

Parrott's focus between now and March is clear, getting back to Seville and "putting the ball in the back of the net" for Real Betis as he has done so well for Republic of Ireland in the past year.

Shania Twain is standing up for others in country music.

The legendary star in the genre used her acceptance speech for the Equal Play Award at Sunday’s CMT Awards to call for more equity and diversity in the country music industry.

“When I wrote the phrase ‘Man I feel like a woman’ I honestly had no idea at the time it would become an undercurrent of a decades-long career,” she remarked, referring to one of her biggest hits. “It’s amazing how one statement can empower so many.”.

The phrase, Twain mentioned, “has been adopted by an array of fantastic communities all around the world and become a genuine path of power…which brings me so much joy.”.

It has been revealed that “I believe in an all-inclusive country music. We’re family,” Twain said. “This is a genre of music with a rich history that raised and nurtured my own songwriting and performance and recording career from childhood. Currently, the industry standard does a real disservice to this.”.

Twain, who was presented the award by rapper Megan Thee Stallion, shouted out some of the diverse acts she is spotlighting on her “Queen of Me” tour this year, including Lily Rose, Lindsay Ell, Hailey Whitters, Mickey Guyton and others.

“I will continue to do my best as a trailblazer,” Twain remarked. “Together, let’s ensure all our fellow artists get equal play regardless of gender, age or race.”.

Industry observers note that she also performed acappella with the African American singing group, The BoykinZ, while presenting an award onstage. Twain connected with the group, who are sisters and rising country stars, after Kelly Clarkson surprised them recently by bringing Twain out to meet them during an episode of Clarkson’s daytime talk show.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Few topics in Germany spark as many heated debates as integration.
  • It has been revealed that every two years, the government's Commissioner for Integration presents a comprehensive set of statistics on the matter.
  • Speaking in Berlin on Wednesday, Pawlik offered an overall positive assessment: "Integration is improving steadily, despite ongoing hurdles and challenges." She continued: "The people of our country want integration to succeed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few topics in Germany spark as many heated debates as integration. How successful have efforts been to integrate fresh arrivals? What is needed to enable successful integration? And what are the biggest problems?

It has been revealed that every two years, the government's Commissioner for Integration presents a comprehensive set of statistics on the matter. Since last year, that role has been held by Natalie Pawlik, a parliamentary representative from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD).

Speaking in Berlin on Wednesday, Pawlik offered an overall positive assessment: "Integration is improving steadily, despite ongoing hurdles and challenges." She continued: "The people of our country want integration to succeed. They rightly expect that people who live in Germany permanently will learn our language and abide by our laws.".

The Commissioner for Integration is part of the Federal Ministry of Labor because ensuring that newcomers find work quickly is especially important.

Industry observers note that the integration reportwas created by a team led by Frank Kalter, director of the German Center for Integration and Migration Research (DeZIM), drawing on official government statistics, surveys and independent studies. They found that when all immigrant groups are counted, about 30% of the population today has some sort of migration background — even if that comes down to only one parent.

Pawlik commented: "This is an important message at a time when the discussion often focuses primarily on problems related to supposedly failed integration." Kalter also pointed out that the employment rate among immigrants in Germany is higher than in most other EU countries — nearly 70%.

And they work primarily in one sector: "In recent years, the biggest increase of workers without German citizenship has been in the health and social services sector." According to the data, there were about 1.8 million people without a German passport working in Germany in 2009. By 2025, this number had more than tripled to 5.8 million.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, however, problems remain. In nearly all immigrant groups, women have difficulty finding employment, especially if they have children and their husbands are employed. Only about 60% of women in such families are employed, whereas nearly 88% of women in families with German passports are employed.

Sources indicate that there are also immigrant groups that face barriers to accessing educational opportunities and the job market. These are mostly young men who came to Germany as refugees. And if one considers citizenship as a distinguishing factor, the percentage of convicted criminals who are not German citizens is far higher — around 40% — than their share of the population. And they are also reported to the police far more frequently. At the same time, individuals without a German passport are also more likely to become victims of crimes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, pawlik emphasizes that language acquisition is the foundation and starting point of any successful integration. But this is precisely where the government tightened its purse strings earlier this year to save money. Many integration courses are now no longer offered at all or receive less government funding. Pawlik made it clear that she is strongly critical of these cuts, even though she herself is part of the federal government.

Sources indicate that most recently, Pawlik and her fellow Social Democrats have been advocating for people who have been working in Germany for some time to receive more secure residency permits — especially those from Syria and Ukraine. On Tuesday, SPD lawmakers adopted a position paper on the matter. In the paper, they propose that existing legal rights that allow workers to remain in the country should also apply to refugees. In other words, it would give working refugees a more secure status.

But will the conservatives from the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) — who lead the coalition led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) — support this? "You'll have to ask the interior minister," Pawlik replied when asked by DW. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) is known for being a hardliner on immigration policy.

This article was originally published in German.

Jobe has captained England’s Under-21s and, as well as U21 head coach Lee Carlsey, Tuchel acknowledged the influence of Jude on the Borussia Dortmund midfielder’s first senior call.

He flew to England and met Bellingham face to face. It was a secret mission. Watzke was determined not to attract any attention that could jeopardise negotiations.

According to recent reports, the problem: Sunderland, Bellingham’s former club, had secured promotion to the Premier League only a day earlier. Hundreds of supporters were gathered outside the hotel where Watzke and Bellingham were due to meet. To avoid being recognised, Watzke put on sunglasses and a cap before making his way through the crowd. He brought two gifts with him. Firstly, a BVB shirt with Jobe’s name on the back. Secondly, a handwritten note from Kovac expressing his desire to work with the midfielder. A few days later, Watzke received a phone call. It was Jobe. His decision had been made. He was joining Dortmund.

Ever since, the midfielder has enjoyed almost unwavering support. Watzke frequently spoke with him throughout his first season, offering encouragement and reassurance. The same was true of Kovac and other senior figures. Equally important to his breakthrough has been team-mate Felix Nmecha, with whom Bellingham has developed a close friendship and who has become an important source of advice. When time allows, the two enjoy playing padel together. Off the pitch they are opponents; on it they form a midfield partnership.

Recent findings suggest that and while his father Mark was still complaining to club officials around a year ago that his son was not getting enough playing time, the situation has changed dramatically. The Bellingham family are delighted, and his England call-up has provided further confirmation that he is on the right path.

Making the step to the senior team 💪 Thomas Tuchel on Jobe Bellingham 🗣️ https://t.co/kKRR1NcPFR.

Recent findings suggest that fifteen months ago in Austria, Bellingham still needed some convincing before stepping in front of the press. Today, he regularly conducts post-match interviews. He’s leading the way. And in Dortmund they are convinced of one thing: We will be hearing a lot more from Jobe Bellingham.

Industry observers note that very good player, very good season. In the way we play now I don’t see him in a central position in the build-up, more in the finishing position of a No 8 or No 10 and the competition [for those places] is very high in our squad. He is in our squad of 55 and we see his quality. It was close for him.

Sources indicate that we were not happy about this. We could understand the disappointment of the fans with what happened before. This is expressed now and should be a closed book.

Everyone can see how Ben presented himself in the March camp. He did excellent and scored for us then conceded a penalty. Not easy for him but when I speak to him I always feel the hunger to come back. He is the stand-out player for Arsenal in a position where we have a lot of problems [with injuries] somehow, a lot of changes. Every time I watch Arsenal I see a very strong Ben White.

He deserves to open a latest chapter and receive positive feedback from the crowd.

It has been revealed that I think Kobbie has had a difficult spell with his team and club and missed a lot of matches. In the meantime Jobe impressed in that spell. The door is always open for players to overtake and make their mark. That is a sign of the competition for central midfield places.

He is a more defensive player than his brother. Good on the ball, good physique, big body, technical player who can keep possession. It is up to him now. We only have Tuesday and Wednesday to prepare and it will be difficult because [in the last camp] we developed some latest patterns, some new behaviours. It will be hard [for him to pick that up in two days] but it is up to him. He is excited, happy and eager to impress which is the best foundation to have a good camp.

It will be Rio [Ngumoha], who played there for Liverpool and impressed in the last camp. Josh [King] can play there. We will try that. And Morgan Gibbs-White. We need runners there and I think we have options. It was a close call not to bring Noni [Madueke]. It was very close since he got his chance when Bukayo was injured at Arsenal, getting minutes and goals. But we stick with the group we have and give them our trust.

In a recent development, the door is always open and nothing has changed. We decided to do this [camp] without him.

Industry observers note that it’s an incredible achievement [winning the Ballon d’Or and winning a  record-breaking 126th cap] that these two occasions come together in one week. He wins the Ballon d’Or and deservedly so and now his 126th cap. Incredible achievement that underlines his professional status and his demeanour. His attitude. He is our captain. I cannot find a better frame [he means stage] to celebrate his achievement.

In a recent development, let’s not forget that it is a crucial match for us. We are desperate to win and have a final in Spain afterwards. The focus is on Croatia and it is a deserved ‘frame’ [stage] and occasion to celebrate his achievement.

Everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception. We are speaking now about a player who was not in camp and it counts when you miss a camp. As I said last time he misses too many opportunities to impress. It was a long camp, 2½ weeks and the players there used it to build something extraordinary. The credit goes to them and the trust goes to them.

It’s not personal and we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset or not desperate to play for his country. The competition is on and the players who were in camp used their opportunity and have kept their place.

According to recent reports, he has a fantastic character and he impressed us in the US. He gives us a bit of flexibility. We nominated 22 outfield players which gives us flexibility in training. You could call it that he is the ‘extra’ player up front and a young, exciting and flexible player. He can play in the No 10 and No 9 for sure and we would like to see how he can play on the wings. In training [for the World Cup] we tried him at full-back. We won’t try that again!

Recent findings suggest that the attitude, the smile, the positivity and he is difficult to defend against. We hope he can bring that spark to camp.

Lee Carsley is speaking very highly of him for a long time now. He is the captain of the U21s, the stand-out player. I think the door should always be open for the pathway, the door should always be open for special performers over a long period of time and that is what Jobe has done.

He has found his way and his rhythm with Dortmund who have had an excellent start to the season. He is a regular starter there and there is an opportunity because Myles is suspended for the Croatia game.

In a recent development, jobe comes through the pathway and on his own merit and deserves to make an impression for us. That’s why we are delighted he is with us in camp and we can see what he can do for us.

He misses too many opportunities to impress. The trust is for the players who are in camp. It is not personal and we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come in and play, but the players in camp did an amazing job.

It’s enough No10s and we stick to the guys who were in camp. We were happy with the last two-and-a-half weeks we had together. The impact of the players throughout that camp was immense and that is why we stick mainly with the group. We have Josh King in the group who plays there [No 10] but I want to see him on both wings. He covers all eventualities because Josh can play all four positions. That’s basically the reason.

Jude has previously spoken about his dream to play in the same England team as his brother, who is two years younger than him and has also followed his path by playing for Dortmund. Jobe moved there from Sunderland at the start of last season and finished his first campaign in Bundesliga as a regular starter.

“We’ve played together for so long in the street and to play with my brother Jobe for England would be the biggest dream of my life, that would mean more than any of the trophies, nothing would even get close to that. Nothing,” stated Jude two years ago.

Jobe Bellingham’s call-up for the England squad is ahead of Everton’s Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, who has been in eye-catching form for Everton. It also demonstrates that Tuchel is thinking of the future, with Jordan Henderson not picked despite his presence in the World Cup squad.

England checked with Chelsea and were told that Palmer was fit for international duty if selected. “Load management” not an glitch this time, then.

In a recent development, he is doing well. The reason why he has been left out, I don’t know. But we are happy with Phil. It is my duty to help him and slowly, slowly he will be back to his best. We are very happy with Phil.

And the message is plain: miss a camp for reasons with which he does not agree and pay the price.

A clear message to the squad 👊 Watch TT's full interview on the official England app ⤵️.

It has been revealed that I am quite surprised that Noni Madueke has not made the England squad today. He’s on arguably his best run of form in an Arsenal shirt. The winger has started seven of the last 10 matches and has four goal involvements (three goals and one assist) in his last eight appearances. He has been playing well on both flanks, too. Given his importance to Tuchel at the World Cup, it’s a bit of a strange one.

Recent findings suggest that josh is the pride of her club and our supporters. He came to this club at eight. How he’s playing, how he’s performing, we’re really proud of him. I am so happy for him. He’s a really humble kid. He wants to improve every day, a special day for him and all of us.

He is talented, he can receive between the lines where there is no space, he can dribble, he can run, he can pass. We are working with him on his finishing which is the most difficult thing in the game, to score a goal. But his character, he is so mature. He has everything to become one of the best players in the world.

Lee Carsley has been talking highly about Jobe for weeks and months, that he deserves it if there is a spot and a possibility to join and to make an impression in the first team.

He had good matches and is on a good run of form with Dortmund so he deserves to be with us. We have 21 outfield players for the first match and then possibly 22 for the second match. [Lewis-Skelly is suspended for the Croatia match after picking up two bookings in the opening games].

Thomas Tuchel has Jordan Henderson back fit – and playing well – since the last international break. The last of Henderson’s 91 caps came at the World Cup against Panama, with his tournament effectively ended when he famously broke his arm in the celebrations at the Azteca after Mexico were defeated. From Tuchel’s squad in the summer, Djed Spence has also returned from injury although he is only just back playing for Inter Milan.

Marcus Rashford is set to miss out on England through injury having barely played since the last international break. The Manchester United forward pulled out of the last squad, then returned for his club the following weekend. But he has not featured since the defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. His absence will open up a space for another wide forward, with Noni Madueke pushing for a call-up with his form for Arsenal.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of the announcement by Thomas Tuchel of England’s squad for their remaining two Uefa Nations Group 3 matches against Croatia – them again – at Wembley next Thursday and Spain at the Metropolitano in Madrid next Sunday night. England have already qualified for the knockout phase – barring a defeat by Croatia by a margin of eight or more goals – but would need two victories to avoid France and Portugal in the next two-legged phase in March.

Tuchel’s only major injury doubt from the last squad are Arsenal’s Bukao Saka and Como’s Trevoh Chalobah as well as the more long-term absentee Tino Livramento, the man Chalobah replaced in the World Cup 26. Djed Spence has returned to full fitness and played for Inter in their Milan derby defeat last weekend while the head coach’s favourite player, Jordan Henderson, has been passed fit to play for Chelsea at his boyhood club Sunderland on Sunday though at 36 his race may finally have been run at this level despite his unexpected encore in the last 18 months.

For the first time since 2001 England will have the Ballon d’Or winner in the squad and Harry Kane will also become England’s most-capped player – barring some misfortune when Bayern Munich take on Mainz on Saturday – by leading them out at Wembley on Thursday night for his 126th appearance.

Recent findings suggest that whether he will be joined by Cole Palmer in the squad remains the only significant matter of note. The Chelsea forward pulled out of the last squad as part of his club’s management of his groin injury but he has played in their last four Premier League games, scoring once and being sent off once as well. Kobbie Mainoo is fit again and may be picked to see if his backside has recovered from bench splinters since his summer of exasperation.

The squad will be released at 10am and followed by Tuchel’s explanations, which we will also cover here, an hour later.

Belief and bench steer Northern Ireland into Nations League top tier

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Highlights: Northern Ireland secure to promotion to League A.

After going 500 minutes without conceding a goal, Northern Ireland could be forgiven for having to make adjustments to play from behind.

Having travelled to Budapest knowing a point against Hungary would be enough to top Nations League B2, Barnabas Varga's strike after 35 minutes for the hosts at the Puskas Arena altered the picture and, for the first time in the campaign, left Michael O'Neill's side having to chase a game.

Their response to the deficit - on the pitch, from the bench and high in the stands where their suspended manager was watching the game - displayed the best characteristics of a side who had not won at this level before this unbeaten campaign.

While the point from a 1-1 draw in Budapest will be long remembered for Justin Devenny's brilliant equaliser and the scenes of celebration that greeted promotion to the competition's top tier for the first time, it was beyond the highlights and headlines that O'Neill saw the emerging qualities of his side.

It has been revealed that "We went behind tonight and it was difficult, you know? Massive stadium, big atmosphere, but we came out and played well in the second half and got what we needed from the game," mentioned the manager.

"Those are things that I'm very pleased that are in this squad at such a young age. The technical side of the game we'll always look to improve on, but in terms of the physical, the tactical and the mental side of a game, we're very far ahead of where I thought we would be at this time.".

Northern Ireland draw with Hungary to seal Nations League promotion.

Watch: Devenny the hero as NI earn promotion.

Hungary enjoyed more than 70% possession in the first half, and they could have been further than a goal ahead with Liverpool star Dominik Szoboszlai striking the base of the post after only five minutes.

O'Neill made his first change at half-time, bringing on veteran striker Josh Magennis, while Kieran Morrison, Brodie Spencer and Paul Smyth all followed in the second half.

Magennis and Morrison made a real impact before the equaliser, but it was the belief shown by all involved that O'Neill felt was key to the turnaround.

"I felt in the first half from where I was seeing the game, we just looked a little bit leggy which is natural," added O'Neill.

"I just felt we needed that freshness at the right points in the game that helped us, but it was the belief that we could get back into the game, and the belief that we could see the game out.

"I think we showed a lot of attributes that are in this squad at this moment in time and certainly in the second half that was that was the case.".

'I genuinely believe it will only get better' - O'Neill.

For all the plaudits earned by this team who conceded just one goal in six games while picking up 12 points, among the most impressive aspects of the campaign has been who they have had to do without.

Talismanic Liverpool defender Conor Bradley has not played for this side in over 12 months through injury.

Ali McCann is another who missed both 2026 Nations League windows, while influential defender Daniel Ballard featured only in the first game in Georgia before a hamstring injury.

Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill was forced to pull out of the November squad through injury at a time when he would perhaps have been the most natural replacement for Jamie Donley after the striker picked up a second booking against Ukraine last week and had to miss the finale through suspension.

Having taken over an ageing squad four years ago, O'Neill has rebuilt his playing panel with a group that feels as if it is getting deeper with each international window.

"The encouraging thing is we have players on the outside - we've Bradley to come back in, Ballard to come back in, Ali McCann, young Ceadach, Eoin Toal," added the former Stoke City and Blackburn Rovers boss.

"We have good competition for places now. We're going to need that competition, and some players are going to miss out, but we are building depth to the squad that will help us going forward.".

Come the next Nations League, that will be all the way into the uncharted territory of the top tier.
